rules.title: Annual Rent Increase Cap (25%)
rules.requirement: The Rent Control Board cannot approve a rent increase of more than 25% in any one-year period for any tenant, counting all increases from standard rent increases, major improvements, and hardship surcharges together.
rules.key_value: 25% max increase per year (combined across increase types)

coverage_conditions.notes: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from rent increase limits for up to 30 years (or the amortization period of the initial mortgage, whichever is less). Dwellings vacant for 18+ months or substantially rehabilitated (rehab cost exceeding 50% of fair market value, with required Certificate of Occupancy) may be granted a 5-year exemption or unrestricted initial rent.

rules.exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings, substantially rehabilitated dwellings, and long-vacant rehabilitated dwellings may be exempted from rent restrictions for specified periods per Sections 19:2-18.1 through 19:2-18.3.
rules.penalty: Monetary penalty up to $500 (Board) or fine of $100-$2,000 and/or up to 90 days imprisonment upon conviction, per violation.
rules.quoted_span: the Rent Control Board shall not grant increases exceeding twenty-five (25%) percent in any one (1) year for any tenant

rules.title: Rent Increase Cap for Substantially Rehabilitated Vacant Units
rules.requirement: A landlord who rehabilitates a vacant apartment unit by spending at least 12 months' worth of actual monthly rent on the unit may increase the rent by up to 10%, limited to one such increase per unit in any 12-month period.
rules.key_value: 10% max increase, limited to 1 per unit per 12 months
rules.interaction: Operates alongside the general 25% annual increase cap but is a separate, specific allowance tied to documented rehabilitation spending on a vacated unit.
rules.quoted_span: Any landlord that rehabilitates a vacant apartment unit by spending a total amount equal to at least twelve (12) months of actual monthly rent per unit will be entitled to a maximum of ten percent (10%) increase in the actual monthly rent

rules.title: Utility Cost Surcharge Cap
rules.requirement: If a landlord proves heating and water costs rose more than 10% year-over-year, the Rent Control Board Administrator must grant a utility surcharge, but it is capped at a percentage of the monthly rent roll that varies by building size.
rules.key_value: Surcharge capped at 15% of rent roll (≤30 units), 5% (31-200 units), or 3% (>200 units)
rules.exemptions: Surcharge may be denied if the Board finds heat or water is not being provided in conformance with applicable law after the date of application.
rules.interaction: This surcharge is counted together with other increases under Section 19:2-22 when determining if the combined 25% annual cap is exceeded.
rules.quoted_span: the increase allowed shall not exceed fifteen (15%) percent of the monthly rent roll of apartments which contain thirty (30) or fewer units; and the increase allowed shall not exceed five (5%) percent of the monthly rent roll of apartments which contain more than thirty (30) units

rules.title: Prohibition on Retaliatory Eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord may not bring an eviction action against a tenant as retaliation for the tenant's efforts to assert rights under the rent control ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall bring any action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce any right under this chapter.
